created_after: Ghidra mission setter, enum formatter, task-force activity formatter, task-force serializer, naval-side serializer/deserializer, and numeric parser were mined
all retained d29/d49/d50 production frames were decoded and correlated
retained naval body and side windows were searched
same-tick save-oracle reports and game localisation were checked

requirements.why_human_input_is_required: Retained side windows contain only zero oracle examples; the three nonzero rows were never retained with repeated raw qwords.
requirements.input: Complete B6_HUMAN_CAPTURE_CARD.json against a paused same-tick D04 process and melt.
requirements.acceptance: anti_air_fixture_verify.py returns ok=true for all eight rows.
requirements.unblocks: wire signed i64 CNavalCombatant+0x150 as exact per-side anti_air_raw/100000

requirements.why_human_input_is_required: Across 291 admitted frames from 402 retained paired hours, every one of 597 d50 removals occurred only at complete combat teardown; 111 PARTIAL_DATA frames were masked and contained no admitted transition rows. No parent-surviving leave exists to validate the transition independently.
requirements.input: A controlled naval combat capture with one identified ship leaving while the same combat generation remains active for at least two later closed frames. Preserve d29/d49/d50 H4CR, the before/during/after save oracle, member state/slot, ship id, combat id/generation, and the user-issued retreat/disengage action and tick.
requirements.acceptance: Exactly one previously active membership tombstone, no d49 parent tombstone in that frame, parent remains active for two frames, ship identity remains present in d29, and the save/UI oracle independently classifies the action.
requirements.unblocks: prove standalone leave and distinguish it from parent teardown

requirements.why_human_input_is_required: Retained d29 deletions occur in mixed contexts: seven cross a fail-closed gap while the last certified d50 baseline remains active, four follow observed membership removal, and six have no captured combat membership. d29 carries no cause and d50 teardown is not a sinking timestamp.
requirements.input: A controlled single-ship loss fixture with hourly-or-finer d29/d49/d50, terminal naval result/save data containing sunk-object identity, ship name/id/owner, winning side, exact loss hour, and before/after CShip plus combat-member windows. Also capture a deliberate disband/scuttle negative control outside combat.
requirements.acceptance: Sunk and non-sunk deletion causes are mechanically distinguishable by an authenticated engine/result carrier; ship id joins the terminal combat generation with no time-window inference.
requirements.unblocks: typed sinking lifecycle and terminal naval loss replay rows

requirements.why_human_input_is_required: The activity label is a multi-input engine decision tree, and the task-force serializer contains no proved scalar repair-progress or retreat state. Retained snapshots do not contain controlled transitions.
requirements.input: For one stable task_force_id/fleet_id, capture paused before/during/after transitions for moving, docked, repairing, and combat retreat. Preserve full CTaskForce and mission-subobject windows, CShip hull rows, combat-member state/slot, exact UI activity localisation key, issued action, and same-tick save at each stage.
requirements.acceptance: Each activity/repair/retreat output is reproduced from exact authenticated inputs across all stages, including zero/nullable states and a non-retreat combat negative control.
requirements.unblocks: either an exact derived activity producer or a documented not-applicable disposition for mission_state/repair_progress/retreat_state

requirements.why_human_input_is_required: CShip+0x3C and global sunk-convoy history contain counts but no per-loss route identity; retained data cannot join a loss to source/destination without a timing guess.
requirements.input: Controlled convoy route with known source, destination, route/transport identity, escort mission, and one observed combat loss. Preserve the route manager object/window, combat generation, d56 task force rows, global sunk-convoy history, and before/after save at the same game hours.
requirements.acceptance: An engine-carried stable route identity joins the exact loss and survives a no-loss negative-control hour; source/destination are not inferred from current task-force province.
requirements.unblocks: convoy_route_context_id and route-linked replay loss event
